Vocabulary for Negotiating a Deadline

Real phrases and words used by professionals when a client asks for an earlier delivery.

Useful Phrases

I'm afraid that timeline will be very difficult.Signal a problem politely but firmly.
Let me check with my manager and get back to you.Buy time before committing to anything.
We might be able to extend the deadline if more resources are provided.Offer a conditional solution.
If you can be flexible on scope, we can keep the timeline.Propose a trade-off.
Just to confirm, we're agreeing to the delivery schedule as discussed?Check understanding before closing.
We have limited flexibility on this issue.Set a clear boundary without sounding rigid.
Let's try to find a solution that works for both sides.Frame the negotiation as win-win.
I'll send you a follow-up email with the confirmed dates.Close the conversation with a clear next step.

Word Bank

deadlineThe date or time by which something must be finished.
concessionSomething you give up in order to reach a deal.
counterofferA new offer made in response to the other side's proposal.
consensusGeneral agreement reached by everyone involved.
bottom lineThe final, non-negotiable point in an offer.
deadlockA point where neither side can agree, and talks stop.
win-winAn outcome where both sides benefit from the agreement.
trade-offGiving up one thing in exchange for gaining another.

Reference Grammar: First Conditional

Structure

If + present simple, will / can / could / may + base verb

Use it for real, possible situations in business — offers, conditions, and next steps.

If we receive confirmation today, we can arrange transport tomorrow. Real possibility → professional offer
If you confirm the priority list by noon, we will ship those items first. Condition + clear result
If the warehouse is still full, we may need an alternative storage option. Softer modal (may) for uncertainty

Do

  • Use present simple after if (not will).
  • Choose will / can / could / may for the result.
  • Add a comma when the if-clause comes first.
  • Soften hard “no” with an alternative offer.

Don’t

  • ❌ If we will receive the parts…
  • ❌ If the client needed it earlier, we would… (2nd conditional — different meaning)
  • ❌ “No, that’s impossible.” (too direct)
